findings.evidence: grep: `FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:65` uses `ofHom (_root_.Bialgebra.unitBialgHom R H)` inline and `FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:73` only proves `eq_unit`; `rg -n "counit|def unit|abbrev unit|toBialgHom_unit" code/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FiniteTypeTrivial.lean` finds no finite-type counit or named unit API, while Mathlib has `Bialgebra.counitBialgHom` at `mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Hom.lean:350`.
findings.fix: Add public `unit (H) : trivial R ⟶ H` and `counit (H) : H ⟶ trivial R` wrappers using `Bialgebra.unitBialgHom`/`Bialgebra.counitBialgHom`, plus characteristic lemmas such as `toBialgHom_unit`, `toBialgHom_counit`, and non-redundant pointwise forms; define `trivialIsInitial` and `eq_unit` in terms of the named `unit`.
findings.issue: `trivialIsInitial` builds the map `trivial R ⟶ H` inline and the file exposes no named finite-type coordinate `unit` or `counit` morphisms with `toBialgHom`/apply normal forms, despite this object being the terminal/trivial affine-group API.

summary: The finite-type trivial object is exposed, but the coordinate-map API is incomplete: consumers still have to unfold the initial-object proof or rebuild raw Mathlib maps to use the unit/counit maps.
